title: The ring of values of $E$-functions is not a field
summary: Let $\mathbf{E}$ be the ring of values taken at algebraic points by $E$-functions. The exponential function and the Bessel function $J_0$ are classical examples of $E$-functions. We prove that $\mathbf{E}$ is not a field. More precisely, we prove that it is neither noetherian nor factorial, and construct non-units of $\mathbf{E}$ explicity, including $e+1$, $J_0(1)$, and ${}_1F_1(a;b;1)$ for rational parameters $a$ and $b$ such that $0

title: Sparse Lifts of q-Linearized Permutation Polynomials with Explicit Inverses
summary: We give a higher unit-torus lift from q-linearized permutation polynomials over Fqn to generally nonlinear sparse permutation polynomials over Fqns. The construction preserves compositional inverses: if a linearized polynomials and its inverse have coefficients (ai) and (Ai), then the lifted polynomial and its inverse have the same coefficients. As a consequence, we obtain nonlinear binomial lifts whose inverses are again binomials in the two-dimensional case, including an explicit inverse for a binomial family over Fq4. The three dimensional specialization yields permutation trinomials whose compositional inverses are again trinomials, together with explicit involution criteria and examples.

title: Pointwise improvement of the error term in the higher rank hyperbolic lattice counting problem
summary: We prove an upper bound for the error term in the higher rank hyperbolic lattice counting problem for ${\hbox{SL}(n, \mathbb{Z})}$. Blomer and Lutsko achieved recently a significant improvement of previous known results by Duke--Rudnick--Sarnak and Gorodnik--Nevo--Yehoshua. We deduce an improved upper bound for the error which holds for almost all pairs $z,w \in {\hbox{SL}(n, \mathbb{R})}$. We also derive a $Ω$-result for the error term, in the spirit of Rudnick--Phillips.

title: On Solvable Automorphism Groups of Function Fields over Finite Fields
summary: The classical Hurwitz bound gives a linear upper bound for automorphism groups of algebraic curves in characteristic zero, whereas algebraic curves in positive characteristic can have much larger automorphism groups. In this article, we firstly investigate the solvable subgroups and $p$-subgroups of $\operatorname{Aut}(F/\mathbb{F}_q)$ where $p=\operatorname{char}(\mathbb{F}_q)$ and $F/\mathbb{F}_q$ is a function field of genus $g_F\ge2$ with full constant field $\mathbb{F}_q$. We prove that there are explicit constants $C_q^{(\mathrm{sol})}$ and $C_q^{(p)}$, depending only on $q$, such that, for every solvable subgroup $G\le\operatorname{Aut}(F/\mathbb{F}_q)$ and every $p$-subgroup $P\le\operatorname{Aut}(F/\mathbb{F}_q)$, \[ |G|\le C_q^{(\mathrm{sol})}(g_F-1), \qquad |P|\le C_q^{(p)}(g_F-1). \] In particular, one may take $C_q^{(\mathrm{sol})}=12q^2(q-1)$ for $q\ge4$ and $C_q^{(p)}=5q$ for every $q$. In the second part of this article , we give the asymptotic lower bounds for solvable automorphism groups. For every $q$ there is an explicit constant $L_q>0$ and a sequence of function fields $F_i/\mathbb{F}_q$ with $g_{F_i}\to\infty$, together with solvable subgroups $G_i\le\operatorname{Aut}(F_i/\mathbb{F}_q)$, such that \[ |G_i|\ge L_q(g_{F_i}-1). \] For $q\ge5$ one may take $L_q=2q(q-1)/(q-2)$. If $q=r^2$ with $r\ge3$, an unramified tower construction over the Hermitian curve gives the stronger choice $L_q=2r^3(r-1)/(r-2)$. Moreover, as an application of our tower construction above, we improve the lower bound of Ma and Xing to $B_q\ge 2(q-1)/(q-2)$ for $q\ge 5$. As another application, we extend our method for bounding solvable automorphism groups to $p$-solvable subgroups, obtaining explicit linear bounds in terms of the genus.

title: Automorphisms and canonical forms of integer lattices
summary: We improve the Plesken--Souvignier algorithm for computing automorphism groups and isometries of positive definite integer quadratic lattices by exploiting characteristic sublattices and refining vector enumeration. For lattices with roots, we also use the Weyl group to accelerate the computation of canonical forms. Experiments with concrete implementations demonstrate substantial speedups and show that canonical forms can be computed at a cost comparable to that of computing automorphism groups.

title: The WZ pair and finite congruences
summary: We construct a meromorphic Wilf--Zeilberger pair for the hypergeometric series for \(3\ln 2\), completing the WZ proof left open by Guillera and Rogers. The same pair yields a one-parameter identity and, after a half-integer shift and differentiation, an inverse-binomial series for \(ζ(3)\). We also study the finite truncations of the logarithmic series. For every prime \(p\ge 5\), we prove that the lower truncation is congruent to \(q_p(2)-1\) modulo \(p\), while the upper truncation is congruent to \(-\frac{7}{16}p^2B_{p-3}\) modulo \(p^3\). The proofs combine the WZ method with terminating hypergeometric identities, the Pfaff--Saalschütz identity, and classical congruences for harmonic sums.

title: CM fibers of Shimura parametrizations and thirteen proofs of the class number one theorem
summary: We determine thirteen entirely CM identity fibers of Shimura parametrizations attached to elliptic curves of rank two and conductor below $2000$. Each yields a proof of the imaginary quadratic class number one theorem. The argument combines the Gross--Zagier formula with the Ribet--Takahashi degree comparison to show that the fiber is completely explained by known CM points.

title: Distribution of central values of Hecke $L$-functions of $n$-th order characters
summary: We prove a one-sided central limit theorem for $\log |L(\tfrac 12,χ)|$ in a thin family of $n$-th order Hecke characters, for $n \geq 3$. The proof combines the method of Radziwiłł and Soundararajan with a recent asymptotic formula of Diaconu, Ion, Paşol, and Popa for the twisted second moment with a power-saving error term. We also obtain upper bounds of the conjectured order of magnitude for the $2k$-th moments for $0< k< 1$.

title: A Half-Constant Upper Bound for Chowla's Cosine Problem
summary: Let lambda(n) denote the infimum of -min_x sum_{a in A} cos(ax) over all sets A of n positive integers. While the classical Sidon-difference construction yields lambda(n) <= (1 + o(1))sqrt(n)/2, we construct sets achieving a leading constant of 1/2: lambda(n) <= (1/2)sqrt(n) + O(n^(1/4)sqrt(log n)), establishing limsup_{n->infinity} lambda(n)/sqrt(n) <= 1/2. This construction combines a two-sided Sidon square identity, a Singer difference set, a Fejer-kernel majorant, a parity-biased deletion, and an exact-cardinality probabilistic selection. We also provide an L^4 criterion and a multiplicity bound constraining any construction with a smaller leading constant. In the opposite direction, we incorporate the L^1 norm into Bedert's boundary estimate with an explicit constant, yielding two lower bounds for f_A(x) = sum_{a in A} cos(ax): (1) -min f_A >= cn^(1/4) for every n-element set A subset of [1, Cn]; and (2) (-min f_A)^3 ||f_A||_1^2 >= cn for every n-element set A subset of N. The second bound recovers the 1/5 exponent of Bedert and Shankar and improves it whenever ||f_A||_1 is small relative to -min f_A. Numerical values of the construction are reported up to |A| = 25,440.

title: Holonomic sequences arising from meromorphic modular forms
summary: We introduce a systematic framework for constructing holonomic recurrences from meromorphic modular forms. Its central ingredient is a modular analogue of creative telescoping, which turns finite-dimensional quotients of spaces of meromorphic modular forms into explicit recurrence operators. This provides a common explanation for several previously isolated examples: it recovers Apéry's recurrence, Beukers' modular constructions and Zagier's seven sporadic recurrences. The framework also produces a large collection of new examples across different weights and groups. The modular origin of these sequences also confers them with non-trivial arithmetic properties, such as denominator bounds, irrationality statements, and $p$-adic congruences.

title: An Enhanced Higher Green's Function on the Modular Curve
summary: The higher Green's functions $G_{k/2}(z,w)$ on the modular curve are real-valued eigenfunctions of the hyperbolic Laplacian in each variable, with logarithmic singularities along the diagonal. Gross and Zagier conjectured that their values at CM points, after multiplication by suitable powers of the discriminants, are logarithms of absolute values of algebraic numbers. The conjecture was proved by Li, Bruinier, and Yang. Mellit proposed a complex refinement of this conjecture, predicting that the normalized CM values of a complex lift of the Green function are logarithms of algebraic numbers modulo periods. For $Γ=\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)$ and $k\in{4,6,8,10,14}$, we follow Zagier's construction of CM invariants from Eichler integrals of the Eisenstein series $E_4$. By applying Maass raising operators in both variables to a normalized iterated Eichler integral of a Bergman-type kernel, we obtain a complex-valued extension $\mathcal G_{k/2}^\bullet(z,w)$ whose real part is a constant multiple of $G_{k/2}(z,w)$. We study the normalized CM values of $\mathcal G_{k/2}^\bullet$ and describe their dependence on the choice of representatives of quadratic form classes. In particular, we show that replacing the quadratic form corresponding to the first variable by an equivalent one changes the exponential of the normalized value only by a root of unity. We also prove the algebraicity of these exponentials in the special case where the second CM point is $w_*=(1+i\sqrt d)/2$, with $d>3$ and $d\equiv3\pmod4$, and the class of the quadratic form corresponding to the first variable is equal to its inverse.

title: Likely and unlikely ramification of algebraic points on curves
summary: This paper initiates the study of arithmetic properties of closed points of arbitrary degree on curves. We show that a pointless curve of rank $0$ can have only finitely many cyclic degree $\ell$ points for all sufficiently large primes $\ell$. More generally, we show that the residue fields of points on curves of genus at least $2$ and rank $0$ are often biased away from total ramification. The proof technique illuminates a natural intermediate conjecture between the Manin--Mumford conjecture and the Zilber--Pink conjecture for self-products of abelian varieties. This intermediate conjecture implies analogous results for other splitting profiles.

title: Denominators in the Farey Sequence, the Stern Sequence, and the Frobenius Problem with Relatively Prime Multipliers
summary: The Frobenius problem asks, given two positive, relatively prime integers $a$ and $b$, what is the maximum integer that cannot be expressed as a linear combination of $a,b$ using non-negative coefficients? This problem is resolved. However, if we add the restriction that the coefficients themselves must also be relatively prime, we create an open problem with connections to the Stern and Farey sequences and the Jacobsthal function. We prove that under this new restriction, a maximum inexpressible integer still always exists, and explore its values and properties as functions of $a,b$.

title: Arithmetic jet spaces and the unramified Zilber--Pink conjecture for subvarieties of abelian varieties
summary: We show how the methods of delta geometry can be used to bound the degree of points in the Zilber--Pink locus of a subvariety of an abelian variety, if the varieties are defined over a number field and we restrict to points with bounded ramification at a fixed prime.

title: Higher derivatives of the Gram function
summary: We study the nonlinear phenomenon of the asymptotics of higher-order derivatives of the Gram function $t_u$. We also prove the uniform distribution and continuous uniform distribution modulo one of $t^n_u$ for $n = 1, 2, \dots$. We use AI to formalize our proofs in Lean.

title: Roth's theorem on weighted projective lines
summary: Let ${\mathbb P}^1_{\mathfrak q}$ be the weighted projective line with coprime weights ${\mathfrak q}=(q_0,q_1)$ and $L=q_0q_1$. The weighted Veronese map $Φ\colon {\mathbb P}^1_{\mathfrak q}\to {\mathbb P}^1$ satisfies $h\circΦ=L\,{\mathfrak s}$. Pulling back Roth's theorem gives the optimal exponent $2L$ for the full rational orbit set. For points represented by coprime integral coordinates, counting suggests the smaller exponent $q_0+q_1$. We formulate this as a conjecture and prove an $S$-adic radical form under the $abc$ conjecture. For ${\mathfrak q}=(2,3)$ the resulting inequality at the target $[1:1]$ is the coprime Hall-type inequality, and Danilov--Elkies examples show that the exponent $5$ is sharp. We also prove the expected exponent unconditionally over characteristic-zero function fields for constant targets and polynomial approximants, and for almost every real target. A weighted $abc$ formulation is introduced; in signature $(3,2)$ finitely many coefficient pairs are equivalent to $abc$, and weighted Belyi maps transfer this input to arbitrary algebraic targets. Applications include a pullback form of Schmidt's subspace theorem, weighted Thue inequalities, and a counterexample to a naive weighted rescaling of Roth's index construction.

title: The local structure of refined class groups in cyclotomic Iwasawa theory
summary: We give an explicit local description of ray class refinements in cyclotomic Iwasawa theory. For distinct primes $p\geq5$ and $\ell$, and even $2\leq k\leq p-3$, we prove that the $ω^{1-k}$-component of the $p$-primary ray class group of $\mathbb{Q}(ζ_p)$, with squarefree modulus supported above $\ell$, is nonzero if and only if $p\mid\ell(1-\ell^k)B_k$. In the cyclotomic tower, we determine the local modules and their correction modulo the diagonal global Tate module, obtaining an explicit determinant formula. Their Frobenius Euler factors, combined with the Mazur--Wiles theorem, yield a ray class form of the Iwasawa main conjecture for nonexceptional odd characters. We also obtain exact class number valuation comparisons at every layer, including those before stabilization, recover Finat's formula for $\ell=2$, and deduce refined $μ$-vanishing from Ferrero--Washington. The cyclotomic character explains the Wieferich exception, while existing Eisenstein congruence theorems connect the divisibility criteria with prime-level Ramanujan-style congruences.

title: Simultaneously preperiodic points and colliding orbits for families of polynomials in characteristic $p$
summary: Let $k=\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$ and let $f\in k[X]$ be a polynomial of degree at least $2$ such that $f-f(0)$ is non-additive. For $α,β$ in an algebraically closed extension $L$ of $k$, we prove that there are infinitely many $λ\in L$ for which both points are preperiodic under $f(X)+λ$ if and only if $α,β\in k$ or $f(β)-f(α)\in E_f$. Here $E_f=\{c\in G_f:(f-f(0))^n(c)\in G_f\text{ for every }n\ge0\}$, where $G_f=\{c\in k : f(X+c)-f(X)\in k\}$. We also provide a necessary and sufficient criterion for the corresponding colliding orbits set to be infinite.

title: A sharp lower bound for the sextic large sieve
summary: We establish a matching lower bound for the sextic large sieve over the Eisenstein integers in an unbalanced range, with both indices restricted to squarefree ideals. Let $Ξ_6(A,B)$ denote the squared operator norm of the sextic residue-character matrix with row and column norms at most $A$ and $B$, respectively, outside a fixed finite set of primes containing those above $6$. For every fixed $0<δ<3/11$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, we prove $Ξ_6(A,B)\gg_{δ,\varepsilon}(AB)^{-\varepsilon}A^{5/6}B^{1/3}$ for $B^{16/11+δ}\le A\le B^{2-δ}$. Consequently, the full-cutoff norm satisfies $Ξ_6(X,X)\gg_\varepsilon X^{17/16-\varepsilon}$. The main difficulty is to preserve the large second moment supplied by Gauss sums when the column moduli are restricted to be squarefree. We prove a second-moment formula uniform in the prime exclusions and character twists arising from Möbius inversion, and use it to show that the squarefree projection retains a positive proportion of the original moment. A separate argument combining cubic and sextic large-sieve bounds then transfers the lower bound to squarefree rows.

title: Yau's number-theoretic conjecture and sharp spectral bounds for quantum harmonic oscillators
summary: We prove Yau's number-theoretic conjecture on positive integral points in real right simplices in every dimension $n\ge3$, and apply the resulting sharp polynomial bound to quantum harmonic oscillators. The lattice-point bound holds for every choice of positive real intercepts for which the count is nonzero, with equality precisely when all intercepts equal the same integer. For oscillators in dimensions $n\ge3$, we obtain explicit upper bounds for eigenvalue counts and spectral remainders for arbitrary positive frequencies at every threshold at or above the lowest eigenvalue. For frequencies with rational ratios in dimensions $n\ge2$, an additional lattice coordinate and interpolation give bounds for energy sums, or first Riesz means, at every threshold. When all frequencies are equal (the isotropic case), the oscillator attains these bounds: the counting bound is exact at its energy levels, and interpolation on its natural energy grid recovers the energy sum at every threshold. In three dimensions, the exact formula displays the periodic contribution associated with the resonance discussed by Fefferman and Seco. The proof builds on the slicing method of Yau and Zhang. Arithmetic and geometric consequences include explicit bounds for smooth numbers and lattice-point discrepancies.

title: A recurrence in logarithmic Möbius sums with coprimality conditions via Euler--Maclaurin
summary: We derive a recurrence for logarithmically weighted Möbius sums by combining Möbius inversion with the Euler--Maclaurin summation formula. Consequently, starting from estimates of orders zero, one and two, we obtain polynomial approximations for these sums for every nonnegative integer exponent of $\log$. We then extend these estimates to sums with coprimality conditions via a convolution identity and to sums weighted by the reciprocal of the sum-of-divisors function. We also establish the nonnegativity of the latter sums for every positive integer logarithmic order, proving that they never change sign.

title: Fine structure of even Galois deformation rings
summary: For every even Galois representation in a family of prime conductor $\ell$, we prove that if $k \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$ is maximal such that \[\ell \equiv 1 \bmod 3^k\] then the even mod $3$ deformation ring $R_S \otimes_{\mathbb{Z}_3} \mathbb{F}_3$ of level $S=\{\ell,3\}$ does not have a quotient isomorphic to $\mathbb{F}_3[T]/(T^{2+3^{k-1}})$. As a corollary, we deduce that the global even deformation rings $R_S$ are finite and flat in the category of $\mathbb{Z}_3$-modules.

title: A generating function identity for finite and symmetric multiple zeta values via Dougall's bilateral ${}_2H_2$ summation
summary: We establish a generating function identity for finite and symmetric multiple zeta values using Dougall's bilateral ${}_2H_2$ summation formula. As an application, we prove a restricted sum formula in which the parity of each component of the index is prescribed. We also derive a generating function identity for finite multiple zeta values $ζ^{}_{\mathcal{A}}(\{1,2\}^n)$ and symmetric multiple zeta values $ζ^{}_{\mathcal{S}}(\{1,2\}^n)$, thereby proving Kaneko's conjecture for finite multiple zeta values and its symmetric analogue.

title: On Berndt-Straub conjectures about zeros of generalized Ramanujan polynomials
summary: We settle two conjectures of Berndt and Straub asserting that all nonzero zeros of the generalized Ramanujan polynomials $R_k(x;χ,ψ)$ and $S_{2n}(x;χ,χ)$ lie on the unit circle for real nonprincipal Dirichlet characters. We prove their conjecture for $R_k$. For $S_{2n}$, we prove that at most four nonzero zeros lie off the unit circle, all purely imaginary. If $χ_{163}=\left(\frac{\cdot}{163}\right)$ is the primitive quadratic character modulo $163$, then $S_6(x;χ_{163},χ_{163})$ has four exceptional zeros, showing that this bound is sharp. This disproves the second conjecture and establishes that the `Riemann hypothesis for period polynomials' can fail for Eisenstein newforms. Further, we introduce a transcendental invariant whose sign determines whether exceptional zeros of $S_{2n}(x;χ,χ)$ occur in all sufficiently large degrees, and show that these zeros converge to transcendental limits off the unit circle. For primitive odd characters, we relate this invariant and these limits to Fekete polynomials.

title: A certified classical-strip comparison for the de Bruijn-Newman constant
summary: We give a directed comparison beginning with the classical zero strip \(\lvert\Ima z\rvert\le1\) for the de Bruijn--Newman heat deformation. Under explicitly stated complete model-to-function source, localisation and global contact premises, translated-probe estimates imply \[ Λ\le\frac{148611789321711}{10^{15}} =0.148611789321711<0.148612. \] The construction uses Raymond's finite source data and 57 fixed translated kernels, independently checked by rational Bernstein certificates. An explicit finite Weyl estimate improves the positive first-head tail and its centred logarithmic moment. A centred cone transfer retains the original physical error allowances, exceptional debit and additive cone reserve, and charges the change in existing phase-surplus credits. Directed tail enclosures are regenerated at 192 and 256 bits; a separate exact-rational auditor accepts all 19,023 comparison steps. The controlled decrease from the complete two-source comparison is \(0.000021760452379\). We also prove a compatible matched logarithmic tail transfer and identify the finite requirements for stronger exponent pairs. A supplementary section records Raymond's ceiling below \(0.116398\) under the distinct \(7/8\) zero-free hypothesis.

title: Counting matrices with given characteristic polynomial
summary: Let $f$ be a monic polynomial of degree $n$ with integer coefficients. We use Fourier analysis to prove a new upper bound on the number of $n\times n$ matrices with characteristic polynomial $f$ and integer entries in $[-T,T]$, as $T\to \infty$. The implied constant in our bound only depends on $n$ and is otherwise uniform in $f$. Our bound improves on recent work of Habegger, Ostafe and Shparlinski for $n\geq 4$.

title: Higher rank elliptic sieve via CM endomorphisms
summary: A theorem of Landau and Ramanujan states that almost all integers are not sums of two squares (when ordered by their absolute value). Equivalently, almost all integers are not norms from the Gaussian rationals $\mathbb{Q}(i)$. In this paper, we prove a version of this norm result for elliptic curves $E$. Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over a number field $K$ with complex multiplication, such that $K$ contains the endomorphism ring of $E$. For a fixed non-torsion point $P \in E(K)$ and an abelian extension $L/K$, we show that subject to a technical condition, the $y$-coordinate of almost all multiples of $P$ does not belong to the norm group of $L$. The proof is an adaptation of an argument of Bhakta et al. , whose main tools are elliptic divisibility sequences and a sieve technique known as the elliptic sieve. To account for the points in $E(K)$ arising from the additional endomorphisms, we apply the elliptic sieve to elliptic nets, a higher-rank generalisation of elliptic divisibility sequences. This approach demonstrates the possibility of applying the elliptic sieve to $\mathbb{Z}$--linear combination of points on elliptic curves and the usefulness of elliptic nets to counting problems on elliptic curves.

title: Untrodden pathways in the study of partitions with parts separated by parity
summary: In this paper, we study a partition function with parts separated by parity from a family of partition functions introduced by Andrews in 2019. We first show that its generating function admit representation in terms of mock modular forms of weight $3/2$. We then initiate a study of smallest-part partition function analogues of partitions with parts separated by parity, which, to the best of our knowledge, has not previously been investigated in the literature. We show that the generating functions of these smallest-part partition functions are likewise expressible in terms of mock modular forms, mock Maass theta functions and Zagier's $q$-series $H(q)$, which he describes as a ``half-derivative of the Dedekind eta-function". Our study also leads to new combinatorial interpretations of the coefficients of the aforementioned mock modular form, function $σ^*(q)$, and mock theta functions $ψ(q)$ and $A(q)$ in terms of odd Ferrers graphs. Moreover, we provide a quantum $q$-series identity involving Ramanujan's famous $σ(q)$ function. We also derive the leading asymptotic term of one of these partition functions, whose generating function we first express in terms of $σ^*(q)$.

title: A Combinatorial Proof of Partition Identities for the Number of Distinct Part Sizes
summary: In 1984, Bressoud and Subbarao established an interesting weighted partition identity connecting the partition function and the divisor function. Recently, the first author, jointly with Bhoria, Eyyunni, and Maji, extended the work of Bressoud and Subbarao and obtained the following analogous weighted partition identity. For any $n \in \mathbb{N}$, they obtained \begin{equation*} p^{(2)}(n) = \sum_{π\in \mathcal{D}(n)} (-1)^{ \# (π) }s(π) \left( \ell(π) - s(π) \right). \end{equation*} In the present paper, we provide a combinatorial proof of the above identity and extend the result for $p^{(k)}(n)$, where $p^{(k)}(n)$ denotes the number of partitions of $n$ into exactly $k$ distinct part sizes.

title: On Permutations Whose Adjacent-Sum Reciprocals Sum to One
summary: In this paper, we give a constructive proof that for any integer n>7 (resp. n>6), the numbers 1,2,...,n can be arranged in a circle (resp. in a line) such that the sum of the reciprocals of all adjacent sums equals 1. The above conjecture was originally posed by Zhi-Wei Sun. Partitioning the integers according to n mod 12 into nine residue classes, we prove a recursive proposition and inductively construct new examples. Main lemmas and propositions in introduction are proved in Section 2. The rest of the cases are handled by explicit constructions in appendix.

title: Some applications of the quasi-Riemann hypothesis to class groups and small generators of number fields
summary: We prove an effective version of the Chebotarev density theorem, conditional on the quasi-Riemann hypothesis for the Dedekind zeta function. Drawing on recent breakthroughs of OpenAI and Cureton--Thorner, we make unconditional the Ellenberg--Venkatesh bounds on $\ell$-torsion in class groups of number fields and extend an averaged result of Lemke Oliver--Smith to arbitrary families of degree-$d$-fields. Further applications are given to the least prime splitting and to small generators in number fields.

title: Linking numbers and special differential characters in arithmetic hyperbolic manifolds
summary: We construct non-holomorphic Siegel modular forms whose coefficients encode linking numbers in arithmetic hyperbolic manifolds of simplest type. Our proofs rely on an improved understanding of the transgression forms appearing in Kudla--Millson theory, and along the way we establish some structural properties including in particular their expected current equations.

title: Wendt's determinant and finiteness of prime characteristics for permutation binomials
summary: For $f(X)=X^r(X^s+a)\in\mathbb F_{p^m}[X]$, with $m,r,s\geqslant1$ and $a\in\mathbb F_{p^m}^\times$, put $g=\gcd(s,p^m-1)$. We prove that, for each fixed $g$, only finitely many prime characteristics $p$ admit such permutation binomials, even as $m,r,s,a$ vary. If $6\nmid g$, every such $p$ divides Wendt's determinant $W_g=\operatorname{Res}_X(X^g-1,(X+1)^g-1)$, which is nonzero. When $6\mid g$, this determinant vanishes; inverse power sums and iterated resultants yield an explicit nonzero integer divisible by every such $p>2g+1$. We determine the exact admissible characteristics for $1\leqslant g\leqslant10$, obtain a further divisibility condition over prime fields, and show that in prime fields $g=11$ occurs precisely when $p=23$.

title: Geometric bounds on norms of signed indecomposable integers
summary: We establish bounds on the norm of signed indecomposable integers in totally real number fields, via a geometric argument. We also improve the bound on the norm of totally positive indecomposable integers in real quadratic fields by Tinková and Voutier.

title: Counting quaternion extensions by multi-heights
summary: We prove a case of a conjecture of Gundlach on the number of Galois extensions over $\QQ$ with bounded multi-invariants for the group $G=Q_8$. We also obtain results when imposing local conditions at the wildly ramified place. As an application, we prove asymptotics for the number of $Q_8$-extensions with bounded product of ramified primes.

title: Satisfiability and freezing in random integer programs
summary: We study a model of a random centrally symmetric polytope and ask about the existence of points in the polytope with non-zero, integer coordinates. Our main results are the location of a sharp threshold for the existence of these integer points, a characterization of the typical empirical distribution of their coordinates, and showing that near the feasibility threshold these integer points are almost always totally isolated --- at linear Hamming distance to the nearest other integer point in the polytope. The behavior of these random integer programs is related to that of the symmetric binary perceptron (the case when coordinates of points are $\pm 1$-valued). The lack of symmetry in the set of potential solutions leads to new questions and phenomena, such as the distribution of the coordinate sizes in typical solutions, and requires the development of new information-theoretic techniques to deal with higher-dimensional optimization problems arising in the method of moments.
comment: Minimal AI usage. Comments welcome. 49 pages

title: Overlap distributions under the Gibbs measure of a Haar model of $\log|ζ|$ on and near the critical line
summary: We study the Gibbs measure of $H(h) = \Re\sum_{p^{j} \leq X}U_{p}^{j}/(j p^{j(σ+ i h)})$, a random field modeling large values of the log-modulus of the Riemann zeta function on and near the critical line, where the $U_{p}$ are independent and uniformly distributed on the complex unit circle. Writing $t = \log \log T$, the cutoff $X$ and real part $σ$ may vary with $T$ subject to $T^{1/t^Φ} \leq X \leq T^{1/t^φ}$ and $0 \leq σ- 1/2 \leq C_σt^Φ/\log T$, for fixed $Φ\geq φ> 1/2$ and $C_σ > 0$. On $I_θ = [ - (\log T)^θ,(\log T)^θ]$, define the Gibbs measure $G_{β,σ,T}^{\mathrm{H}}(\mathrm{d}h) := e^{βH(h)}\mathrm{d}h/\int_{I_θ}e^{βH(h')}\mathrm{d}h'$. For every fixed $θ> - 1$ and inverse temperature $β> 0$, the limiting joint distributions of correlations (overlaps) among points sampled from this measure are determined after averaging over the Haar phases. At and below $β_{c}(θ) = 2\sqrt{1 + (θ\vee 0)}$, the limiting two-overlap distribution is concentrated at $q_{0} = |θ\wedge 0|$. Above this threshold, it assigns masses $β_{c}(θ)/β$ and $1 - β_{c}(θ)/β$ to $q_{0}$ and $1$, respectively, and the limiting joint overlap distribution is described by a Poisson-Dirichlet process of parameter $β_{c}(θ)/β$. Approximate Ghirlanda-Guerra identities are shown to hold uniformly for bounded deterministic functions of the sampled positions. This paper is the first in a series devoted to extending these results to $\log|ζ|$ near the critical line.

title: Entropy, isoperimetry and the total variation profile of random walks
summary: The total variation profile $\mathrm{TV}_n$ of a random walk measures how far its distribution at time $n$ is from being invariant under the generators. Three lower bounds are given: an elementary bound $\mathrm{TV}_n \geq 1/\big(44\,L(n)\big)$ in terms of the speed $L(n)$; a bound by the entropy increment $H(P^{n+1}) - H(P^n)$, which is a reverse Pinsker inequality; and a bound in terms of the entropy and the isoperimetric profile. Deciding whether the entropy-increment bound always improves on the isoperimetric one is related to conjectures on the growth of the entropy and of groups. The motivation comes from the question of whether the distributions of a random walk can be transported back onto their translates at bounded cost.

title: Determinantal linear spanning forests
summary: We introduce a determinantal linear process on the space of $1$-forms over a weighted graph endowed with a unitary local system, which we call the determinantal linear spanning forest (DLSF). This process is the analog of the uniform spanning tree in the presence of an arbitrary rank $n$ quenched gauge field in ${\rm U}(n)$ (or ${\rm O}(n)$, ${\rm SO}(n)$, ${\rm SU}(n)$, ${\rm Sp}(n)$), and generalizes the determinantal random cycle-rooted spanning forest which corresponds to the case of ${\rm U}(1)$ and ${\rm SU}(2)$. We describe the support of this process by means of a polymatroid which is described in terms of the circular and bicircular matroids. We also explain how the DLSF relates to the computation of currents in an electrical network in the presence of a gauge field. The partition function of the DLSF is shown to be the determinant of the twisted Laplacian, for which we also give a matrix-tree type theorem that computes its characteristic polynomial. We initiate the study of the twisted Laplacian determinant as a functional on the space of connections, and give a first order expansion of it in a neighborhood of the trivial connection, for which we provide a probabilistic interpretation. We extend the construction to infinite graphs, exhibiting the analogs of the classical wired and free distributions on spanning forests. We give a sufficient geometric condition on the local spectral gap for the existence of a Poincaré inequality as well as the uniqueness of the infinite volume measure, and the exponential decay of correlations. We show that on any recurrent graph, the wired and free DLSF coincide. We construct examples where they do not, for example, unlike in the classical case, on $\mathbb Z^d$ for $d\geq 3$.

title: A Randomized Approximation Algorithm for Doubly Free-Boundary Macdonald Processes
summary: We construct an approximate sampler for finite doubly free-boundary Macdonald rail-yard processes with Macdonald, boundary, and edge parameters in $(0,1)$. The construction allows arbitrary finite sequences of additions and removals of horizontal or vertical strips and all four boundary types. It reverses a finite commutation--reflection history from a partition sequence whose entries are equal, with the common partition weighted by both boundaries. We derive local reconstruction kernels from the skew Cauchy, Littlewood, and branching identities. Bulk and boundary updates combine integer increments with conditional shape sampling at a prescribed size; same-sign swaps use finite conditional resampling. For $K$ reflection periods and an initial partition-size cutoff $M$, the algorithm terminates almost surely and samples the resulting approximating law exactly. We prove total variation convergence to the target process as $K,M\to\infty$ and give explicit bounds for both truncation errors, decaying geometrically in the cutoffs for fixed input parameters. Under fixed parameter bounds, we also bound the expected operation count of direct enumeration in a unit-cost model. We further construct an exact rejection sampler for the initial partition law without a size cutoff or evaluation of its normalizing constant. Using this sampler removes the size-truncation error, leaving only the error from the finite reflection history.

title: The $R_\infty$-nilpotency degree of some lollipop GBS groups
summary: We say that a group $G$ has the $R_{\infty}$ property if the number $R(\varphi)$ of twisted conjugacy classes is infinite for any automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$. The $R_{\infty}$-nilpotency degree is the least integer $c$ such that $G/γ_{c+1}(G)$ has property $R_{\infty}$; in case this integer does not exist, we say that $G$ has infinite $R_\infty$-nilpotency degree. In this paper, we determine the $R_{\infty}$-nilpotency degree of some lollipop GBS groups by using different approaches, such as Sylow subgroups, normal forms and presentation of nilpotent quotients, and diagrams of exact sequences. We also compute the $R_\infty$-nilpotency degree of all 2-generated lollipop GBS groups and of all GBS groups whose associated graph is a tree.

title: Almost tight asymptotic enumeration of finite $p$-groups: Almost all finite groups are $2$-groups of class $2$
summary: Let $f(n)$ denote the number of isomorphism classes of groups of order $n$. We prove, uniformly over all primes $p$, that \[ \log_p f(p^m)=\frac{2}{27}m^3-\frac49m^2+O(m), \] with an absolute implied constant. This improves the classical upper bounds of Sims (\emph{Proc. Lond. Math. Soc.}, 1965) and Newman--Seeley and matches Higman's lower bound (\emph{Proc. Lond. Math. Soc.}, 1960) through the quadratic term. We also prove that \emph{the proportion of $2$-groups of nilpotency class $2$ among all groups of order at most $n$, counted up to isomorphism, tends to $1$ as $n\to\infty$.} These results answer questions~22.3 and~22.19 of Blackburn--Neumann--Venkataraman (\emph{Enumeration of Finite Groups}, 2007). Our proof refines Sims' enumeration framework using graded Lie brackets, constraints on deeper commutator coordinates, and incidence and Fourier estimates for alternating forms. Normalization by changes of generating bases then determines the quadratic term in the upper bound. We also prove that all but a $p^{-Ω(m^2)}$ fraction of groups of order $p^m$ have a central elementary abelian Frattini subgroup. Combining this concentration with the sharp enumeration bound of Bläser--Li--Qiao--Rogovskyy (\emph{arXiv}, 2025) for $p$-groups of Frattini class $2$ yields the linear error term. The same presentation estimates give fixed-quotient extension bounds which, together with Pyber's prescribed-Sylow theorem and the concentration result, establish domination by $2$-groups of nilpotency class $2$.

title: Twisted Equations and Palindrome Length
summary: Twisted equations in free groups are equations in which a finite group of symmetries acts on the free group by automorphisms and anti-automorphisms, such as inversion and reversal; moreover, the variables may be subject to rational constraints. Algorithms from the theory of equations in virtually free groups solve such equations in PSPACE, but they are intricate. Our main result is an elementary algorithm for quadratic twisted equations, which extends the algorithm of Comerford and Edmunds (1981) for quadratic equations in free groups to the twisted setting and to rational constraints. Besides deciding solvability in PSPACE and yielding EDT0L descriptions of solution sets, our algorithm computes, for every quadratic expression, finitely many parametric forms describing its values as freely reduced words. As an application, we study the palindrome length of elements of free groups, that is, the least number of palindromes whose product they are. Guided by the parametric forms that our algorithm computes for products of palindromes, we found, and then proved directly, a characterization of the freely reduced words of palindrome length at most $n$ in terms of patterns describing how palindromes are nested by twisted conjugations, thereby confirming a Catalan structure conjectured by the second author. Consequently, these words form a context-free language, and palindrome length is computable in cubic time as well as in LOGCFL, answering a question of Bardakov, Shpilrain, and Tolstykh (2005).

title: Sylow $2$-Subgroups of Finite Groups with a Single Conjugacy Class of Involutions
summary: We solve Brauer's Problem 33 by determining the finite $2$-groups that occur as Sylow $2$-subgroups of finite groups with a single conjugacy class of involutions. Besides the Sylow $2$-subgroups arising from the relevant non-abelian simple groups in Table 1, these are precisely the homocyclic, generalized quaternion, and Suzuki $2$-groups. The classification of finite simple groups is used in this paper.

title: Stabilizers and maximal subgroups of topological full groups
summary: We study closed-set stabilizers in topological full groups of minimal effective ample groupoids with Cantor unit space. For almost finite or purely infinite groupoids, we extend the maximal stabilizer theorem of Grigorchuk and Vorobets to every subgroup containing the commutator subgroup. For a nonempty closed nowhere dense set, maximality of its stabilizer is equivalent to minimality of its stabilizer action, minimality of the regular reduction, and primeness of a canonical wide open subgroupoid. Without assuming almost finiteness or pure infiniteness, we prove spatial rigidity for stabilizers acting minimally on infinite closed nowhere dense sets. Their isomorphism types determine the ambient Kakutani equivalence class and, when Hausdorff, the effective reduction. We also realize every AF groupoid with compact unit space as the full restriction, with its relative topology, of any minimal effective ample groupoid with Cantor unit space to a closed nowhere dense subset. Combining rigidity and realization yields continuum many pairwise nonisomorphic stabilizers in every subgroup containing the commutator subgroup; these stabilizers are maximal when the ambient groupoid is almost finite or purely infinite. The realization also gives explicit AF subquotients of the ambient reduced groupoid $C^*$-algebra, including the CAR algebra, with compatibility on the canonical diagonal subalgebras.

title: Three-point orbits of 2-transitive groups and their combinatorial applications
summary: Let $G$ be a finite $2$-transitive permutation group. We determine the orbits of $G$ on the unordered triples of its point set, together with the three-point stabilizer and its image inside $S_3$, for every affine and almost simple family in the finite $2$-transitive classification. These data classify the $G$-invariant triple systems and the simple $2$-\mbox{$(v,3,λ)$} designs admitting $G$, and yield in a uniform way the standard objects attached to them: the incidence and block graphs (with arc-transitivity and strong regularity in the Steiner case), the constant-weight and design codes, and the Schurian coherent configurations on triples.

title: Regular automorphisms of periodic $p'$-groups need not be splitting
summary: For a fixed prime $p$, a group is called a $p'$-group if the orders of all its elements are coprime to $p$. It is well known that in a finite $p'$-group an automorphism of order $p$ is regular if and only if it is a splitting automorphism of period $p$. In the Kourovka Notebook, V.\,D.~Mazurov asked whether these two notions coincide for periodic $p'$-groups. We answer this question in the negative by constructing a periodic group of prime period $q$ that admits a regular automorphism of order $p \neq q$ which is not splitting.

title: Minimal Product Sets in Finite Metacyclic Groups
summary: Minimum product-set problems ask how small a product of two subsets of prescribed cardinalities can be in a finite group. Although the problem is completely understood for finite abelian groups, exact results in the nonabelian setting are available only for particular classes. We determine the minimum product-set function $μ_G$ for every finite metacyclic group, without assuming that the relevant cyclic extension splits. Our proof converts the extremal problem into a finite recursive arithmetic description of the feasible cardinality vectors of subset trios. The recursion combines the subgroup structure of finite metacyclic groups with the structural classification of maximal critical subset trios. The resulting characterization recovers the previously known formulas for abelian and nilpotent groups, dihedral groups, and nonabelian groups of order $pq$. It also yields metacyclic examples in which the minimum product-set size lies strictly between the classical lower and upper arithmetic bounds for finite solvable groups. For faithful split metacyclic groups, we further show that requiring one factor to be symmetric, contain the identity, and generate the whole group can force a strictly larger product set than the unrestricted minimum. The latter constraint admits a vertex-isoperimetric interpretation on connected Cayley graphs.

title: The theory of $(λ,μ)$-fold factorizations of groups
summary: Motivated by the recent study of $λ$-fold near-factorizations of finite groups by Kreher, Li, and Stinson (Designs, Codes and Cryptography, 2026), we introduce and systematically investigate $(λ,μ)$-fold factorizations of finite groups, with particular emphasis on the abelian case. These structures form a natural relaxation of $λ$-fold near-factorizations and encompass several related families that have previously been studied in different contexts. We establish the foundational theory of $(λ,μ)$-fold factorizations, provide two general constructions, and prove several nonexistence results for finite abelian groups.

title: A non-nilpotent localization of a finite p-group
summary: We give negative answers to two questions of Farjoun about localizations of groups. For every odd prime $p$, we construct a finite $p$-group $G$, an infinite non-nilpotent group $H$, and a local embedding $f\colon G\hookrightarrow H$. The associated localization satisfies $L_f(G)\cong H$, showing that localizations need not preserve nilpotence and that the localization map $G\to L(G)$ need not be surjective when $G$ is a finite $p$-group.

title: Nonarchimedean discrete groups and quasi-isometric doubles of free groups
summary: For any nonarchimedean local field $k$, we exhibit the first examples of Zariski-dense, discrete subgroups of special linear groups over $k$, which are not commensurable to any lattice in the points of a semisimple group over a local field, and contain an infinite index subgroup isomorphic to a lattice in the $k$-points of a higher rank $k$-semisimple group. We prove that any Gromov-hyperbolic double of a non-elementary free group along a cyclic subgroup embeds as a quasi-isometrically embedded subgroup of $\mathsf{SL}_5(k')\times \mathsf{SL}_5(k')$, where $k'$ is a discretely valued field. More precisely, $k'$ is the field of rational functions $k(t)$ equipped with the Gauss valuation and $k$ is any nonarchimedean local field of characteristic not equal to $2$ or $3$.

title: Multivalued Groups and Schur Rings
summary: We study finite involutive multivalued groups associated with Schur rings. Their reduced valency is shown to equal the least common multiple of the sizes of the basic sets of the corresponding ring. We prove that the double-coset group associated with a complemented subgroup of a finite group is isomorphic to a Schur multivalued group over the complement. In particular, every coset multivalued group is a Schur multivalued group. Using affine Schur rings, we construct families of pairwise nonisomorphic commutative multivalued groups over elementary abelian groups. We obtain asymptotic bounds for the sizes of these families and prove that the proportion of double-coset groups in them tends to zero.

title: On the local Frattini subgroup of a finite group
summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $π(G)$ be the set of prime divisors of $|G|$. For each $p\in π(G)$, choose a Sylow $p$-subgroup $G_p$ of $G$. The subgroup $Ψ(G)= \prod_{p\in π(G)} Φ(G_p)_G$ is called the \textit{local Frattini subgroup} of $G$. Here, for $J \leqslant G$, the symbol $J_G$ denotes the core of $J$ in $G$. The subgroup $Ψ(G)$ is a characteristic subgroup of $G$ that is contained in $Φ(G)$, the Frattini subgroup of $G$. We prove that $Ψ(G)$ satisfies many properties similar to $Φ(G)$. Let $J$ be a normal $p$-subgroup of $G$ with $J \leqslant Φ(G)$, and let $S$ be a Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G$. John S. Rose proved that if $J \leqslant \mathbf{Z}(S)$, then $J \leqslant Φ(S)$. So, in fact, $J \leqslant Φ(S)_G \leqslant Ψ(G)$. Kaplan, Lev, Mann, and Solomon found various other conditions that would ensure $J$ is contained in $Φ(S)$. In this article, we add a few more conditions to this list.

title: On a Combinatorial Characterization of Abelian Group Actions
summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of order $n$ and $X$ a finite $G$-set. We give a necessary and sufficient condition on $G$ for any $X$ to be determined up to isomorphism by certain combinatorial data. Specifically, if $M_H^X$ is the number of $H$-orbits in $X$, and $a_d^X$ is the number of $G$-orbits in $X$ of cardinality $d$, we characterize when equalities $M_H^{X_1} = M_H^{X_2}$ and $a_d^{X_1}=a_d^{X_2}$ for all $H \leq G$ and $d|n$, respectively, force an isomorphism $X_1 \simeq X_2$. Our main result is that this occurs if and only if $G$ is cyclic or $G$ is the direct sum of a finite cyclic group and a cyclic group of prime order. We conclude with an arithmetic application to $L$-function factorization.

title: Profinite recognition of uniformity
summary: Let $G$ be a semisimple Lie group that is not isogenous to the isometry group of real or complex hyperbolic $n$-space. We show that the rational rank is a profinite invariant for irreducible lattices in $G$, unless $G$ has type $D_{2n}$ which forms a genuine exception. In particular, profinitely isomorphic lattices in $G$ of type $D_{2n}$ can have differing virtual cohomological dimension. As another corollary, uniformity is a profinite property for irreducible lattices in $G$ outside type $D_4$. Assuming CSP, the existence of triality symmetries gives uniform and non-uniform profinitely isomorphic lattices in type $D_4$.

title: An explicit construction of a limit variety of groups
summary: We construct an explicit countable group \(G_*=N(R)\rtimes A\) whose generated variety is a limit variety of groups: it has no finite identity basis, whereas every proper subvariety is finitely based. Here \(A\) is relatively free in the variety of groups of nilpotency class at most two and exponent dividing four, and \(R\) is an explicitly defined quotient of the group algebra \(\mathbb F_2[A]\). The proof establishes an ascending chain condition for coefficient spaces indexed by six ordered commutator entries and reduces every proper subvariety to a hereditarily finitely based approximation. Non-finite basability is obtained by transferring independent identities from the constructions of Gupta and Krasilnikov. The resulting variety is contained in \(\mathfrak B_4\mathfrak B_2\). This construction provides the first example of such a variety in which both the generators and a basis are explicitly given.

title: On a finite group in which every non-supersolvable maximal subgroup is a TI-subgroup
summary: We provide a complete characterization of a finite group in which every non-supersolvable maximal subgroup is a TI-subgroup, which generalizes some known related results.

title: Complete mappings stabilizing Sylow $2$-subgroups in central quotients of special linear groups
summary: A complete mapping of a finite group $G$ is a permutation $θ$ of $G$ such that $x\mapsto xθ(x)$ is also a permutation of $G$. Complete mappings have applications in cryptography, particularly in the design of round functions for cryptographic systems. The study of their parity has led to the question of which finite groups admit complete mappings of both parities. A useful approach to this question is to construct complete mappings stabilizing suitable subgroups, in particular Sylow $2$-subgroups. We show that, for every $n\geq2$, every prime power $q$, and every $Z\leq Z(\mathrm{SL}_n(q))$, the group $\mathrm{SL}_n(q)/Z$ admits a complete mapping stabilizing a Sylow $2$-subgroup if and only if $(n,q)\neq(2,2)$.

title: Zero divisors in group algebras of torsion-free groups in odd characteristic
summary: A recent preprint constructs a finitely presented torsion-free group $G$ with a finite two-dimensional classifying space such that $\mathbb F_2[G]$ contains nonzero zero divisors. We extend this to every odd prime $p$: there is a finitely presented torsion-free group $G_p$, again with a finite two-dimensional classifying space, such that $\mathbb F_p[G_p]$ contains nonzero elements $α,β$ with $αβ=0$. Together with the case $p=2$, Kaplansky's zero-divisor conjecture therefore fails over every field of positive characteristic. The new ingredients are a signed version of the parity cancellation, made possible by a bipartite random model on one side; a type design built from the projective plane over $\mathbb F_{p^3}$ with $p$ additional letters, which makes every cross-intersection congruent to $1$ modulo $p$; and a squared-word decay estimate for this design, proved with an explicit test vector. The geometric part of the argument is taken from the characteristic-two construction. The characteristic-zero case remains open.

title: Matrix Waring Problem-III
summary: Let $n,k$ be positive integers and $q$ be a prime power. We prove that there exists a real constant $C_k$ depending only on $k$ such that if $ \# M_n(\mathbb{F}_q) > C_k$ then every element in $M_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$ is a sum of two $k$th powers, proving Larsen's conjecture.

title: $\mathrm{CS}\mathfrak{X}$-groups and free constructions
summary: Let $\X$ be a variety of groups. A group $G$ is $\CSX$ if its maximal $\X$-subgroups are malnormal. We prove that the amalgamated free product of two $\CSX$-groups with a malnormal amalgam and without any involutions is again $\CSX$. Using this, we describe conditions under which the HNN-extension of a $\CSX$-group is $\CSX$.

title: Groups with the fixed-point property
summary: We propose the study of the class of groups that fix a point for every continuous action on any convex compact space. Oliver completed the corresponding program of classifying the finite groups that have this fixed-point property in finite dimensions. Turning to infinite groups, the Schauder--Tychonoff theorem establishes that the integers have the fixed-point property, but this has not been shown for any other infinite, finitely generated group. We establish a local transfer principle and use it to show, as a proof of concept, that $\mathbf{Z} \times (\mathbf{Z}/p\mathbf{Z})$ belongs to this class of groups.

title: The one percent property for free groups
summary: We prove that for every $\varepsilon >0$, there is $δ>0$ such that for every probability measure $μ$ on a free group $\mathbb{F}$, if the operator norm of the action of $μ$ on $L^2\mathbb{F}$ by convolution exceeds $\varepsilon$, then there is a coset of an abelian subgroup of $\mathbb{F}$ with $μ$-mass at least $δ$.

title: Finite groups with conjugacy classes of size $2p^n$
summary: We extend Burnside's $p^a$-Theorem on conjugacy classes of prime-power size by proving that no non-abelian finite simple group possesses a conjugacy class of size $2p^n$ for any prime $p$ and $n\geq 0$. Based on this, we partially extend a well-known result of L. Kazarin by showing that, given a finite group $G$, the subgroup generated by a conjugacy class $x^G$ of size $2p^n$ where $x$ has odd order, is a solvable normal subgroup of $G$. If instead the subgroup $\langle x^G \rangle$ generated by such a class $x^G$ is non-solvable (which forces $x$ to have even order), then $p= 5$ and $\langle x^G \rangle/S(\langle x^G \rangle)$ is isomorphic to the symmetric group $S_5$, where $S(\langle x^G \rangle)$ denotes the solvable radical of $\langle x^G \rangle$.

title: A note on the proof of nonamenability of F
summary: The goal of this note is to provide a human written exposition of OpenAI's recent proof that Thompson's group F is nonamenable.

title: Lie groups are countably representable
summary: We prove that every Lie group can be realized by permutations of a countable set, answering a classical question of Ulam. The key deformation construction originated in an argument produced by OpenAI's GPT 6 Astra during extended mathematical discussions.

title: When do lazy and invertible cellular automata generate all cellular automata?
summary: Let $G$ be a group and let $A$ be a set with at least two elements. A lazy cellular automaton over $A^G$ acts as the identity except at the cells where a fixed pattern occurs, where it replaces the central symbol by a fixed different symbol. Let $M(G;A)$ be the submonoid of $\mathrm{CA}(G;A)$ generated by the lazy and the invertible cellular automata. We study when $M(G;A) = \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$. Since no lazy cellular automaton is surjective, every surjective element of $M(G;A)$ is invertible; hence $M(G;A) \neq \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$ whenever $A$ is infinite or $G$ has an element of infinite order. Moreover, if $|A| = 2$ and $G$ has a quotient isomorphic to the Klein four-group $C_2 \times C_2$, then $M(G;A) \neq \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$. For locally finite $G$, and in particular for finite $G$, these are the only obstructions: we prove that $M(G;A) = \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$ if and only if $3 \leq |A| < \infty$, or $|A| = 2$ and $G$ has no quotient isomorphic to $C_2 \times C_2$.

title: Constructions and automorphisms of quandles
summary: We prove that if M is an abelian group and X = Alex(M, phi) is a Latin Alexander quandle with id - phi in Aut(M), then Aut(X) is isomorphic to M semidirect C_Aut(M)(phi), Inn(X) is isomorphic to M semidirect <phi> and Out(X) is isomorphic to C_Aut(M)(phi)/<phi>. As a consequence, we obtain a description of the automorphism groups of direct products of the cyclic commutative medial quandles C_{2n+1} and the dihedral quandles R_{2n+1}, and we find their orders. Furthermore, we correct a result of Bardakov-Fedoseev [Algebra and Logic 63 (2024), no. 2, 111-142] on multiplication of quandles and prove that the Borodin-Neshchadim-Simonov and Markhinina-Nasybullov quandles can be constructed from conjugation, core, and generalized Alexander quandles, using the operation of multiplication of quandles. Finally, we consider the quotients of a quandle Q, namely the medialization Q^med, the commutativization Q^com, and the trivialization Q^tr. We prove that the conjugation quandle Conj(G) is medial if and only if gamma_2(G) <= Z(G); we find bounds for |Conj(G)^med| and prove that Core(G)^com is isomorphic to Core(G/<<g^3>>). We describe commutative generalized Alexander quandles and, as a consequence, find the commutativization of the dihedral quandle: R_n^com is isomorphic to R_gcd(n,3).
